chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Using idle weeks in the theater to rehearse
summary: During five weeks in the theater McRae and Jeff rehearsed the book and the other sections joined.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Because you remember when we was in the theater, oh about -- we was in the theater about five weeks. We wasn't doing nothing.
What we had to do, just sit around in the theater after the show do nothing? I was new in the band, so we started rehearsing.

I told Jeff, 'Look, Jeff, why don't we rehearse after one show so we can go through the books and clean up a lot of things. So when we get on the one nighters, I'll have some idea what's in the book.'
Because we was going to play a couple of hotels -- play the (inaudible) in Albany. We was heading that way to play the two weeks in Albany. I say let's clean up the book.
Jeff say, 'Okay.' (Foots Inaudible) was willing, the other boy was willing. So we started working.
And the reed section began to sound good, man. I mean it was sounding big and boy we got our tones together. Everybody was together.
Then Jonah Jones heard us, so they

started rehearsing. Then the trombones -- the trombones and the brass I heard (inaudible).
But when they came into the Strand Theater that year, they had a beautiful write-up. The man say it was the best sounding band that Cab --

We were playing behind the band. We were playing -- I did ... the (inaudible) Cab drivers. I think we did this thing 'I'll Be Around.' We were playing! I mean, everybody was really together -- like a new life had got to the band.
Because what they were doing when I walked over there, the band was just there, you know. You find a lot of bands like that.
(Inaudible) they got a job and they come to work and they play the man's music, you know.
